extracted.intended_audience: general readers (unmarried readers, poets, coffee-house literati)
extracted.subtask_description: An 18th-century Spectator essay offering practical counsel to unmarried readers on selecting a spouse (with related asides on poetic taste, the publication of dreams, and evaluating news/rumour in coffee-houses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate reported statements by attending to nonverbal cues
rubrics_metrics.description: In relations, the force of the expression often lies more in the look, the tone of voice, or the gesture than the words themselves; when repeated by the undiscerning, words bear a different interpretation from their original meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that narration grounded on authority and uttered with vehemence may be exaggerated; interrogate credibility by noting the teller's manner and by testing particular points rather than accepting the whole story. Example anti-pattern: repeating a vehement report verbatim without checking the teller's gestures or tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sceptical contravention to detect unreliable narrators (wagering tactic)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a narration is heated and authoritative, one may contest the single way the narrator fixes the matter and point out the many other possible ways it could have happened, thereby exposing embellishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tactic increases the probability of catching falsehoods (author used wagers to profit from this), but requires delicate management to avoid escalating disputes into violence. Scoring note: effective when the narrator is carried into the marvelous or impossible by their passion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the figure of attention in social listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Good breeding obliges a man to maintain the figure of the keenest attention even when inattentive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a coffee-house, the proper posture to appear attentive is leaning over a table with its edge pressing hard upon the stomach; the more pain, the more gracious the bending—this convinces the narrator that you are absorbed. Anti-pattern: obvious inattention that offends social decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish types of liars: embellishers vs reciters
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two sorts of liars: those with impudence and strong memory who merely repeat what they hear (reciters), and those who add good understanding and smooth language and can eloquently embellish certain heads (embellishers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize reciters by literal repetition; recognize embellishers by polished, topical eloquence. Practical use: judge reliability accordingly—embellishers invent details; reciters propagate errors uncritically.

rubrics_metrics.name: When taking descriptive reports, allow the informant to compose themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: A newsman reported asking an advertiser to compose himself before dictating the description of an offender, because anger distorts a person's description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recording descriptions given in anger; let people calm down so the real description (e.g., of a runaway apprentice or wife) is not eclipsed by deformity of the angry speaker. Anti-pattern: publishing a legally significant description while the informant is agitated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish only your own dreams (caveat on publishing visions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer decided to print only dreams of his own invention, suppressing many submissions and invoking Epictetus's advice: 'Never tell thy Dreams.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about publishing others' visions; consider dreamer's age, condition, and sex when judging merit. Anti-pattern: filling a speculation book with unsolicited dreams of dubious provenance; editorial policy: limit dream-publication to material likely to amuse readers and suit the periodical's taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not import pagan mythology into serious Christian panegyric
rubrics_metrics.description: When celebrating a great man or writing serious panegyric, it is ridiculous for a Christian author to have recourse to Pagan gods (e.g., making Prince Eugene a favourite of Mars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer truthful depiction of contemporary subject rather than mythological dressing; reserve classical mythology for school exercises, mock-heroic writing, or short allusion. Anti-pattern: letting Apollo/Polypheme/river-gods overshadow the real actions of one's subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit classical fable in mock-heroic; favour local superstition in pastorals
rubrics_metrics.description: Mock-heroick poems may gracefully use Heathen Mythology; pastorals, however, gain natural beauty by substituting local, popular superstition (as Philips did) for antiquated rural deities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match mythological or fabulous machinery to genre: mock-epic = acceptable use; serious panegyric = avoid; pastorals = prefer native, believable elements over classical fawns and satyrs. Example: praise for using shepherds' own superstitions instead of Ovidian machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edict for poems on contemporary political events (no pagan agents)
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing on the Prospect of Peace, the essayist 'strictly require[s]' the writer to remember he is a Christian and not to sacrifice his catechism to his poetry: no Phoebus, no Mercury sent with dispatches, no Minerva imitating plenipotentiaries; the Fates shall not cut threads of life except for rhyme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition of Pagan agents in such poetry except brief metaphor or simile with caution; exception: female poets may retain their gods. Anti-pattern: dramatizing modern diplomacy through dialogues of Jupiter or Neptune as real agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary criteria for choosing a spouse
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief things to regard in choosing a marriage partner are: a virtuous disposition, a good understanding, an agreeable person, and an easy fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh talents, virtue and disposition above mere wealth: a man of excellent talents with moderate estate is preferable to one who is only rich, because faculties may acquire riches while riches cannot buy worthy endowments. Anti-pattern: choosing purely on fortune or superficial wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value good-nature and humanity over mere wit and fashionable genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and the capacity to entertain should not be highly valued except when founded on good-nature and humanity; many ingenious men merely make themselves and others uneasy, addicted to town pleasures and quick sensations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid marrying men who require constant lively sensations and gaiety; prefer those who can reflect with reason and honour and who show gratitude and patience toward a partner. Scoring note: identify men who support their partners' failings with benevolence versus those who 'must necessarily fly to new acquisitions of Beauty.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a man of sense who cultivates his partner's happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: A man of wit and sense who contemplates his partner with reason and honour will supply with good-nature the partner's failings, contrive new pleasures, make her fortune subservient to her honour and reputation, and be grateful for favours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sort produces continual variety and improvement in married life; judge suitors for demonstrated generosity, sobriety, and industry in inventing pleasures rather than mere initial passion. Anti-pattern: a 'fool' who is ungrateful and incapable of appreciating his partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning against dull, insipid husbands
rubrics_metrics.description: A modest woman joined to a dull fellow may be unable to enjoy their fortunes, with long silences and little conversation, relying on servants for small satisfactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid choosing a spouse who lacks imagination and conversation, as this leads to a life at a 'full stop' despite wealth. Example negative outcome: 'Honest Will Thrash and his Wife' who had scarce a word to say to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugal love as higher refinement than gallant amour
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugal love is a much higher refinement than the frivolous affectation of amorous gallantry. Love for a wife cultivates substantial virtues and improves the mind, whereas love for a mistress is like a fever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value friendship, tenderness and constancy dressed in simplicity of expression over extravagant raptures and slavish adoration. Anticipated evidence: letters from men of good-nature to their wives will show more genuine merit than amorous epistles to mistresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praise rising genius by truthful substance rather than classical ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: When discovering or praising rising genius, prefer works that avoid relying on school-boy tales and Pagan fables and that celebrate the subject itself rather than inserting mythological machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage poets to create from their own mind ('make his own Poem') and to avoid borrowing too much from the classics; the best panegyrics carry the colours of truth. Anti-pattern: a poet whose celebrated passages are actually speeches of Apollo or descriptions of Polypheme.
